entries.title: Genesis 44:5
segments: Whereby--he divineth; in this, as in using an interpreter and swearing by the life of Pharaoh, Joseph conducts himself towards his brethren as an Egyptian.  We are not to understand that he actually practised divination.  The practice of divining by cups was common among the Egyptians.

entries.title: Genesis 44:9
segments: Hasty decisions, and strong, confident assertions are often wrong, and bring those who make them into great perplexity and distress.

entries.title: Genesis 44:14
segments: Fell before him; in token of submission.

entries.title: Genesis 44:16
segments:
The iniquity of thy servants; he might not mean by this to confess that they had stolen the cup, but that God in his providence was righteously punishing them for their sins, and that they meant to accept whatever he should lay upon them. 
 
Hearty acknowledgment of the justice of God in our trials, and humble submission to his will, indicate a preparation for approaching deliverance.

entries.title: Genesis 44:18
segments:
Even as Pharaoh; having full power to do as he should choose. 
 
It is never wise or right, in a world of mercy and grace, to despair, or cease to use appropriate means; however dark to human appearance may be the prospect, or feeble the means used, God can give speedy and triumphant success.

entries.title: Genesis 44:32
segments: The most touching and efficacious eloquence is often a simple narration of facts.  God's ways are great, and a true recital of them is suited to produce great effects.  His ways, like himself, are perfect, and a knowledge of them is suited to make men perfect, and lead them, in their measure, to imitate him.

entries.title: Genesis 44:33
segments: Let thy servant abide instead of the lad; the feelings of the ten brethren towards their father and towards Benjamin, the trial of which seems to have been a chief object of Joseph's demeanor towards his brethren, were fully proved by this last self-sacrificing offer of Judah.

entries.title: Genesis 44:34
segments: An affectionate and tender regard for one's father, a readiness to sacrifice, and if need be suffer, to prevent evils from coming upon him, and to prolong his life, promote his comfort, and cheer him in old age, is peculiarly pleasing to God, and is often followed by some of his richest blessings.
